title: Why are manhole covers usually round?

lines.text: Have you ever wondered why almost every sewer manhole cover on city streets is perfectly round?
The answer is an ingenious geometric safety rule.
A square cover can be turned diagonally, making its width shorter than the diagonal hole opening.
lines.caps: A square cover turned *sideways | easily drops through the *hole!

lines.text: If a heavy iron square cover slipped, it would plummet down and crush underground utility workers.
Because a circle has a constant diameter from every single angle, a round cover can never fall into its own hole.
lines.caps: A round cover can *never fall | into its own *opening!

lines.text: Round covers are also vastly easier to move, allowing city crews to simply roll them across the asphalt.
lines.caps: Crews can easily *roll them | instead of lifting 300 *pounds

lines.text: Geometry literally saves lives beneath our city streets every single day.
